g.title: OX06SceneElementIdentity
g.text: OX-06 | GIVE FIRST CITY ELEMENTS SEMANTIC IDENTITY
Behavior board • cycle 145 • DRAFT FOR OWNER REVIEW

g.title: input
g.text: FirstCityComposition remains the source of resolved selected-time scene decisions.
OX-03 composition mapping and OX-04 support / unavailable meaning stay intact.

g.title: identity
g.text: A meaningful First City object has a stable First City identity and a semantic role.
Illustrative names only; no global ID format or reusable registry is chosen here.
Identity is separate from visibility, depth, and the drawing function.

g.title: separate
g.text: Role answers “what kind of object is it?”
OX-05 depth group / local order answers “where does it draw?”
Renderer pass answers “which code draws it?”
One cloud identity may map to two existing cloud passes.

g.title: map->separate
g.text: do not equate object with layer

g.title: stable
g.text: VISIBLE OR HIDDEN AT SELECTED TIME
Existing composition decisions still control whether optional objects appear.
A visibility change does not rename the semantic object or change its role.
SelectedInstant and supplied / carried / unavailable weather meanings stay authoritative.

g.title: passes
g.text: TIME_WASH and READOUT_QUIET_ZONE remain named compositing passes.
They do not receive scene-object identity or change their OX-05 placement.
Background < Middle-Ground < Foreground and all approved sublayer ordering remain unchanged.

g.title: proof
g.text: First City has a finite, reviewable set of meaningful object identities and roles,
with a testable mapping to current draw passes and no universal element registry.
Provide scoped proof or an explicit recorded disposition; make no visual-acceptance claim without installed evidence when applicable.

g.title: bounds
g.text: No renderer or weather-decision changes; no new weather facts or interpolation.
No world-wide registry, scene-pack schema, second world, inspector, hit target,
Moon inspection interaction, readout/timeline change, or artwork redesign.
Those remain separate roadmap outcomes. Board approval does not authorize implementation.
